commands.review_summary:
This PR changes `UsageFormatter.percentText` to return a localized `<1%` label for any positive sub-1 percentage, adds a zh-Hant format override, and extends `UsageFormatterTests` for 0.6% and 0.75% usage lines.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection of current main shows `percentText(0.6, suffix: "used")` formats through `%.0f` to `1% used` before the replacement can fire, while existing tests already define sub-1 `percentString` as `<1%`.

target.title: Show <1% for all sub-1% usage, not just under 0.5%
target.body:
percentText formatted the percentage with %.0f and then tried to rewrite a "0%" substring into "<1%". For usage in [0.5%, 1%) the %.0f rounds up to "1", so there is no "0%" left to replace and the user sees a misleading "1% used" (or "1% left") for a value that is well under one percent.

percentString already handles the whole (0, 1) range correctly, and UsageFormatterTests asserts percentString(0.96) == "<1%", so showing "<1%" across the entire sub-1% range is the intended behavior. percentText was inconsistent with it.

Fix: mirror percentString and return the "<1%" string directly for 0 < percent < 1 instead of format-then-replace. The literal uses an escaped "<1%% %@" key, and the zh-Hant override is added so the one locale that reorders the sibling "%.0f%% %@" string keeps suffix-first word order.

percentText backs the menu card percent label, usageLine, and the CLI renderer, so a value like 0.75% now reads "<1% used" consistently there and in the menu-bar text (which is driven by percentString).

Testing: added regression cases in the (0.5, 1) range to the existing sub-percent usage test. They fail on the old code (produce "1% used"/"1% left") and pass after the fix. Full UsageFormatterTests suite is green (42 tests).
